narrative.northStar: The Quiet Workspace Around a Lit Table
narrative.overview: This is the category standard played straight at full craft, chosen by the owner on 2026-10-13 as a standing exit (seed key 518dfea8; the roll ran degraded with no challengers). The application is a near-black cool-neutral workspace of flat panels, 1px hairlines, one calm blue accent and a system sans, with mono only for records. The scene is a separate namespace: a fixed light ground and eleven authored ink-on-paper colours that the application theme never touches. There is no Tabletop logo, wordmark or brand identity; the favicon is a placeholder. Only what is built is recorded.
keyCharacteristics: Two namespaces: --of-* application tokens (dark default, light theme) and --sc-* scene tokens (defined once, never themed).
Depth by lightness step first, a hairline second, a shadow only for what floats.
One accent meaning yours / what you are acting on; danger reserved for destructive meaning.
Everything measures on a 10px quadrille, the same as the scene grid.
Targets are 40px (30px fine pointer for secondary controls); functional text never under 12px.

rules.name: The Two Namespaces Rule
rules.body: --of-* is the application and may be themed. --sc-* is the scene and is defined once, in tokens.css, by nothing else; theme-boundary.test.ts fails a theme that assigns one.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The blue accent marks the one thing you are acting on or the one primary action on a surface.

rules.name: The Tested Contrast Rule
rules.body: Pairs are tested, not asserted: app/a11y-floor.test.ts is the authority, in every theme.

rules.name: The Twelve Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: No absolute font-size goes below 12px, with no exemptions.

rules.name: The Mono Means Record Rule
rules.body: Mono is for measurement and records, never a costume for technical.

rules.name: The Distance Rule
rules.body: The display route sets its status words at 1.6em and never conveys state by colour alone.

rules.name: The Apparatus Is Outside The World Rule
rules.body: Handles and selection draw on a screen-space layer outside the world transform.

rules.name: The Float Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means this floats over the table; page-level sheets and cards use a hairline and a tonal step.

rules.name: The Named Layers Rule
rules.body: Stacking uses the --of-z-* ladder; no bare integers.

rules.name: The Registry Draws The Chrome Rule
rules.body: Rails, docks and prep sections come from registries filtered by role and posture; an unbuilt feature is absent, not inert.

rules.name: The Quiet At Rest Rule
rules.body: Chrome that can be hidden while the table is in use is hidden or closed by default, and stays keyboard reachable.

dos: Do take every colour, size, radius, space and layer from a --of-* or --sc-* token.
Do keep new scene-facing colours in the --sc-* namespace, defined once in tokens.css, and never in a theme block.
Do make a boundary that has to be perceived to operate at least 3:1, and text at least 4.5:1.
Do state status in a word or shape as well as colour.
Do add a new surface as its own stylesheet part, imported above motion.css.
Do reach for the quadrille: multiples of 10px, with the 2/4/6/8/12/16 inner scale.
Do keep motion short and functional and honour prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't recolour or theme the scene.
Don't build a fantasy costume, enterprise admin software or a chat application with a map attached.
Don't add glows, gradients or a second accent.
Don't invent a Tabletop logo, wordmark, mascot or brand colour; none exists.
Don't draw chrome for features that are not built.
Don't use a bare z-index integer, an odd spacing value, or a font size under 12px.
openDecisions: Decided 2026-10-13: a dimmer neutral mid-tone scene ground with a still-contrasting grid (ADR T010). Open for Phase 2: a per-table ground chosen by the GM, and a Scene's own grid colour and opacity.
Brand and name: working title only; favicon is a placeholder.
Not built: player toolset, layers, initiative and turn strip, selection bar, scene tabs, preview as player, prep thumbnails, display turn order.
